    ===Qwen & Hermes’ pick===

    Pick from 2026-11-02 (Nov 1 week 2026, entries 11/02–11/07)

    Score: 9/10 — direct matches on Topological + Magnon + Theoretical + Skyrmion. This is a personalized recommendation score, rather than a measure of paper quality or coverage across all six interests.

    Title: Magnon superlattices around skyrmions in frustrated magnets
    ID: DOI: 10.1103/fhbj-ykvn
    Authors: Adarsh Hullahalli, Christos Panagopoulos, Christina Psaroudaki
    Date: 11/03 entry in the weekly collection; published on 2 November 2026
    Status: Published in Physical Review Research 8, 043116 (2026). Publication details
    Preprint: arXiv:2601.00363v1, first submitted on 1 January 2026. Selected for its publication this week, rather than as a newly submitted preprint.

    why this pick?

    This paper connects internal skyrmion dynamics and magnon interference to spatial patterns and topological bands. It brings together the real-space topology of skyrmions and the momentum-space topology of magnon bands characterized by Chern numbers, making it a strong match for your interests. Published abstract

    1. Keyword matching across the six interests

    Interest How this paper connects
    Topological Direct match: skyrmion textures and magnon bands with nontrivial Chern numbers.
    Magnon Direct match: magnon modes, interference patterns, and hybridization with skyrmion modes.
    Phonon Not directly addressed.
    Theoretical Direct match: spin models, linear spin-wave theory, and Landau–Lifshitz–Gilbert dynamics.
    Skyrmion Direct match: isolated skyrmions, skyrmion lattices, and the internal helicity degree of freedom.
    Altermagnet Not directly addressed; the frustrated magnet studied here is not identified as an altermagnet.

    These distinctions follow the published abstract and the Model and Methods in the preprint.

    2. Why this over other candidates?

    Paper Directly matching interests Assessment
    Magnon superlattices around skyrmions in frustrated magnets — this week’s pick Topological · Magnon · Theoretical · Skyrmion Connects four interests within a single spin-dynamics problem.
    2611.04347 — Altermagnetism-induced higher-order topological Dirac semimetals in two-dimensional nonsymmorphic systems Topological · Altermagnet · Theoretical A theoretical route to higher-order electronic topology through altermagnetism. The closest alternative if altermagnetism takes priority.
    2611.07807 — Nonlinear Interaction and Topological Selection Rules in two Skyrmion Merging: Emergence of Skyrmionium Textures Topological textures · Skyrmion · Theoretical Uses analytical modeling and micromagnetic simulations to study skyrmion merging. A strong alternative for texture formation.
    2611.04229 — Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3 Magnon · Phonon Uses high-field Raman spectroscopy to investigate temperature-dependent hybridization. A strong alternative for spin–lattice coupling.
    2610.41851 — Magnetic control of reflectionless states and an intrinsic-mode exceptional point in a magnon-phonon coupling system Magnon · Phonon Combines experiments and an input-output model to control reflection zeros and an exceptional point. A strong alternative for non-Hermitian wave control.

    Selection criterion: With no explicit ranking among your six interests, I prioritize the number of directly connected interests and the physical coherence of those connections. This pick offers a theoretical path from magnon–skyrmion interactions to topological bands.

    3. Physical insights from this paper

    • Magnon dispersion sets the pattern’s length scale. Interference between symmetry-related finite-wave-vector modes associated with a Mexican-hat dispersion produces the superlattice pattern.
    • The skyrmion helps select and excite the pattern. It breaks translational symmetry and hybridizes internal modes with extended magnons, enabling excitation by a uniform AC magnetic field. The published paper also reports the same pattern under a local Gaussian drive without a skyrmion, clarifying this distinction.
    • Helicity provides an additional dynamical channel. Breathing modes that are magnetically inactive in linear response can become weakly active through helicity dynamics.
    • The topological bands belong to the skyrmion lattice. The paper reports nontrivial Chern bands inside the first magnon gap. Distinguish this lattice band topology from the periodic interference pattern around an isolated skyrmion.

    These results are summarized in the published abstract. The spin model and computational methods are described in the preprint full text.

    Questions to explore while reading — my interpretation

    What hybrid modes could emerge if magnetoelastic coupling to phonons were added to these finite-wave-vector magnon patterns? Could a similar texture-assisted excitation mechanism operate in an altermagnetic background, and which symmetries would it require? These are possible follow-up research questions connecting your interests, beyond the results established in the paper.

    TL;DR

    This week’s pick connects Magnon × Skyrmion × Topology × Theory within one study. Magnon superlattices around skyrmions in frustrated magnets
